open_points.subject: A04 trial-case validation
open_points.text: "its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports" does not say whether a present expected_outputs object must contain every output port or may contain only a subset, nor whether extra names are refused
open_points.question: What exact set of output-port names must a present expected_outputs object contain?
options: Exactly every output port
Any subset of output ports, comparing only those present
Any subset, including unknown names that are ignored
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly every output port when expected_outputs is present.

open_points.subject: A03 sandbox filesystem
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has "no filesystem beyond its input", while A03 gives it "one private exchange directory" and permits opening any path inside that directory
open_points.question: May agent code create, modify and read arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or may it access only runner-managed input and output paths?
options: Allow arbitrary access within the bounded exchange directory
Expose only runner-managed input and output paths
Expose no filesystem paths to user code
open_points.default_guess: Allow arbitrary access only within the bounded exchange directory.

open_points.subject: A03 printed output
open_points.text: "Nothing the code prints or raises is interpreted by the kernel" and "never stdout" do not say where stdout and stderr go or how they are bounded
open_points.question: How must the runner handle stdout and stderr so printing cannot block, exhaust host storage, enter logs, or escape the output bounds?
options: Discard both streams to a bounded sink
Capture and discard up to a release ceiling
Treat any write as a sandbox violation
open_points.default_guess: Discard both streams without logging them, using a bounded nonblocking sink.

open_points.subject: A03 resource-limit precedence
open_points.text: "a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, output_bytes) — resource_exhausted" requires a limit hit to win even when Python code catches MemoryError, OSError or another denial and returns successfully, but no observable hit channel is specified
open_points.question: How does the parent determine that a catchable memory, process or scratch limit was hit?
options: Instrument each limit and report every denial to the parent
Classify only an externally observable termination or over-limit measurement
Let a caught denial disappear and classify the returned result normally
open_points.default_guess: Instrument the runner so every resource denial is irreversibly reported to the parent.

open_points.subject: A03 output-byte accounting
open_points.text: "The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every value output" while resource_exhausted is checked before contract_violation, but malformed values may be impossible to canonicalize
open_points.question: How is output_bytes evaluated when a returned value is non-JSON, cyclic, contains a non-finite number, or otherwise cannot be canonicalized?
options: Classify it as contract_violation without applying output-byte precedence
Measure an intermediate serialization and allow resource_exhausted to win
Treat canonicalization failure as crashed
open_points.default_guess: Classify non-canonicalizable returned values as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: A16 token-list reload
open_points.text: M27 says "a configuration repeating [an agent name] is refused at start", but A16 says "Exactly three checks apply to a re-read" and duplicate agent names are not one of them
open_points.question: What happens when a live token-list reload introduces two agents with the same name?
options: Refuse every request until names are unique
Accept the reload because only the three listed checks apply
Merge the entries sharing the name
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the reload and every request until agent names are unique.

open_points.subject: A16 token comparison
open_points.text: "The kernel compares it in constant time with the owner token and with each agent token" does not say whether every comparison must run or whether comparison stops after a match
open_points.question: Must authentication compare the request token against the complete configured token list before deciding?
options: Always compare against every configured token
Stop after the first constant-time equality match
Use a separate constant-time indexed lookup
open_points.default_guess: Compare against every configured token before deciding.

open_points.subject: A17 credential references
open_points.text: The configuration carries "the reference that resolves to its value on the host", while rule 2 mentions a "secret file", but no reference syntax, path resolution, ownership, permission or symbolic-link rule is given
open_points.question: What credential-reference forms are valid, and what filesystem security checks apply when resolving one?
options: Only an absolute regular file owned by the kernel user with no group/other permissions and no symlinks
Any readable file path
A named host-secret provider rather than a file path
open_points.default_guess: Allow only an absolute, non-symlink regular file owned by the kernel user and inaccessible to group or others.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory startup checks
open_points.text: "The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise" does not define private
open_points.question: Which owners, file types and permission bits are accepted for the data directory, database, value area, fixtures and spool?
options: Require kernel ownership and no group/other permission bits
Require only that other users cannot write
Rely on successful access and the exclusive lock
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel ownership and no group or other permission bits on every entry.

open_points.subject: A18 global store order
open_points.text: Many rules use "the store's one order of records", but no rule defines how positions are allocated when one transaction writes several records
open_points.question: Is there one durable, unique, monotonically increasing position for every record, and in what order are positions assigned to records created by the same store call?
options: One global sequence with an explicit per-operation write order
One sequence per table with a tie-breaker
Transaction positions only, with records in one transaction unordered
open_points.default_guess: Use one global monotonic sequence and specify the record order for every multi-record store call.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization
open_points.text: "Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive" does not define arrival order for requests accepted concurrently by the MCP transport
open_points.question: What observable event establishes the total order of concurrent requests?
options: A sequence assigned when a complete request is received
The MCP transport's own delivery order
Whichever handler acquires the store lock first
open_points.default_guess: Assign a sequence when each complete request is received and process by that sequence.

open_points.subject: M28 and A08 manifest revision
open_points.text: The manifest is read from a location "at the configured manifest_revision", but the texts do not say how that revision is selected or verified
open_points.question: How must the kernel obtain a manifest file at manifest_revision?
options: Read the blob directly from a version-control repository at that revision
Require manifest_location to be a checkout whose current revision exactly matches
Treat manifest_revision as descriptive and read the current files
open_points.default_guess: Read and verify the repository content at the exact configured revision.

open_points.subject: A08 manifest canonicalization
open_points.text: record_digest is the digest of canonical JSON, but A08 only refuses a record that "is not valid JSON" and does not say how duplicate object members or non-finite numbers are classified
open_points.question: Are manifest records that JCS cannot represent refused, and at which manifest-mismatch check?
options: Refuse them as invalid JSON before inspecting fields
Refuse them as a separate non-canonical manifest error
Apply parser-specific duplicate-key behavior
open_points.default_guess: Refuse any non-JCS-representable manifest as invalid JSON before field checks.

open_points.subject: A09 base URL construction
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute http or https URL with a host, while A09 constructs the target by taking the api_base_url "without a trailing /" and appending the path
open_points.question: Are user information, query strings, fragments and arbitrary base paths allowed in api_base_url, and how are trailing slashes removed?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional normalized base path, with no userinfo, query or fragment
Allow every absolute URL and append textually
Require origin-only URLs with no path, query, fragment or userinfo
open_points.default_guess: Allow an optional base path but refuse userinfo, query and fragment, and remove all terminal slashes before joining.

open_points.subject: A09 multipart field names
open_points.text: A02 places no syntax restriction on port names, while A09 inserts a port name verbatim into `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"`
open_points.question: Which port names are legal for multipart bindings, or how are quotes, backslashes and control characters escaped?
options: Restrict multipart port names to a safe ASCII field-name grammar
Define standards-compliant quoted-string escaping
Refuse only names that require escaping
open_points.default_guess: Restrict multipart port names to a safe ASCII identifier grammar at binding proposal.

open_points.subject: A09 response content encoding
open_points.text: The kernel sends `Accept-Encoding: identity`, but the response rules do not say what happens if a service nevertheless sends a Content-Encoding such as gzip
open_points.question: Are encoded response bodies rejected, decoded before size and schema checks, or treated as raw body bytes?
options: Reject every non-identity Content-Encoding
Decode supported encodings and count decoded bytes
Treat encoded bytes as the response body
open_points.default_guess: Reject any non-identity Content-Encoding as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: A09 incomplete error responses
open_points.text: "no valid final response received" is service_unreachable or outcome_unknown, while a 3xx, 4xx or 5xx is classified "whatever the body's size"; the rules do not cover a valid final status followed by a truncated or reset body
open_points.question: Once valid final headers with a 3xx, 4xx or 5xx status arrive, does an incomplete body retain the status-based outcome or become a missing-valid-response outcome?
options: Classify solely from the received final status and ignore body completeness
Require the error response framing to complete
Use the status only after failure_detail_bytes_max bytes are available
open_points.default_guess: Classify from valid final headers; error-body completeness does not change the outcome.

open_points.subject: A09, A10 and A11 not_applied effects
open_points.text: A09 makes a non-read 4xx an EffectAttempt `not_applied` with NodeExecution `operation_refused`; A13 makes `operation_refused` a terminal node failure, while K-08 and A10 say a send after `not_applied` waits for a fresh approval
open_points.question: Can an effect that received a 4xx be resent in the same run, or is fresh-approval resend limited to an unknown attempt that the owner resolves as not_applied?
options: Only owner-resolved unknown attempts may be resent
Every not_applied attempt, including a 4xx, waits for fresh approval
A 4xx is terminal but a new run may retry it
open_points.default_guess: Limit same-run resend to an unknown attempt resolved not_applied; a direct 4xx remains a terminal operation_refused failure.

open_points.subject: M26 EffectAttempt resolution time
open_points.text: EffectAttempt has `recorded_at`, `concluded_at` and `resolved_by`, and an unknown attempt later changes to applied or not_applied, but there is no `resolved_at` and no rule says whether concluded_at changes
open_points.question: What timestamp represents the owner's resolution, and does resolving an unknown attempt mutate concluded_at?
options: Add and record a distinct resolved_at while preserving concluded_at
Replace concluded_at with the resolution time
Keep the original concluded_at and record no resolution time
open_points.default_guess: Preserve concluded_at and add a distinct resolved_at for the owner's resolution.

open_points.subject: A10 multipart approval identity
open_points.text: State 0 says approval covers the fully built request and "Any difference at send" asks again, while A10 excludes the multipart boundary from both Content-Type and the body description so different wire bodies can have the same request_digest
open_points.question: Must the multipart boundary be deterministic and fixed by the approval, or is boundary variation explicitly outside the exact-request rule?
options: Use a deterministic boundary and include it in the approved request
Exclude boundary variation as an explicit exception
Generate any boundary but include its value and resulting bytes in request_digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic boundary and include the resulting header and wire body in the approved request digest.

open_points.subject: A13 advancement order
open_points.text: The next executable node is ordered by node_id, and A15 orders records for nodes that "become non-executable together", but neither text orders propagation of skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed records relative to ready-node execution
open_points.question: When failure or guard propagation can conclude nodes while other nodes are ready, which records and executions occur first?
options: Repeatedly conclude all non-executable nodes in node order before executing a ready node
Execute the smallest ready node first and propagate only when no node is ready
Choose the smallest node_id across ready and newly non-executable nodes
open_points.default_guess: Choose the smallest node_id across all nodes that can either execute or be concluded without execution.
